institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had been on folkehøgskole just south of Tromsø and wanted to go back to the Arctic. Ideally I wanted to go back to Svalbard, but their courses did not fit my profil and I chose UiT instead. There I could get courses in my field and enjoy all my outdoor. hobbies.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, but the coordinator at UiT was very bad at answering emails. Every time I wrote about something I just got a text copied from the website which I had already read and not understood.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Getting help changing courses and getting help activating microsoft authenticator

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Sometimes you end in large social student housing, other times not.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
I don't quite remember the process, but I remember when I changed a course. I was just emailing with an administrative worker who did it for me since I was not allowed to take the course originally. 
I do remember that I was not let into a course for the first two weeks even though I had signed up for the course so my lecturer had to email everything to me which is quite annoying for all parts.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: help signing up for classes.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just email the exchange coordination or ask for help because it is always difficult to sign up for courses in other universities than your own.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did one BA course as an elective and two MA courses as restricted electives.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar with lectures and exercise classes. The classes were much smaller than usually so it was more class room style than an auditorium.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Introduction to snow and avalanche science (geo-2015)
2. Physics of remote sensing (fys-3001)
3. Deep learning (fys-3033)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all three of thumbnut I did not have any previous experience in deep learning which made it very difficult for me.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All different kinds of sport and clubs for different things such as board games and choir.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did climbing and tried out choir and enjoyed both of those.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to different places in Troms with friends and see the wonderful nature that is everywhere

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy since Denmark and Norway are very similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The Norwegians are not very extrovert and open so you have to be the one asking to hang out. Once you are friends with them they are really really good friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Making Norwegian friends.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How they don't plan weeks in advance. They plan things on the day or the day before. Much more relaxed and less stressful than in Denmark.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Get out and enjoy the wonderful nature!
2. Remember your grades don't get transferred so take your time to try new things outside school. 
3. January is long and dark but the sun will return quickly and then you get energy to do things all day and all night. Enjoy this but remember your sleep in May and June :)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The exam period is a loooong period with written exams (mine was March 6th-May 8th) and then oral exams after that. The exam period differs in alle courses but I didn't have classes during must of that time so I was very good to have friends before I started the exam period since that had to be done alone.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to let go of my academic striving for good grades. I was very difficult but I have enjoyed finally relaxing a little more about grades since they don't get transferred.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My greatest challenge was balancing my written exam period along with skiing and during social activities. It was a very long exam period (especially since I'm used to maximum two weeks) so I found it difficult keep the motivation high. Being social and going on trips was a must for me.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
